name: Agriculture
blurb: Vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, and autonomous equipment at commercial scale, tracked through USDA ERS, FAO, satellite data providers, and the equipment and standards bodies.

points.desc: Deere's precision agriculture line (See and Spray, autonomous tractors) is the reference commercial deployment.
points.name: Precision ag is shipping product

points.desc: Census BTOS covers agriculture-adjacent sectors in its fortnightly AI-use series.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: The Economic Research Service publishes the data series on precision-agriculture adoption across US farms - variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, autonomous equipment. The federal measurement layer.
points.name: USDA ERS measures US adoption

points.desc: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization's digital agriculture program, with the 60 Decibels-supported Digital Agriculture Index, benchmarks platform adoption and real-world yield and income impact.
points.name: FAO benchmarks digital agriculture globally

points.desc: The AgriFoodTech investment research tracks venture capital into agricultural AI, robotics, computer vision, and farm-management software - the sector's funding barometer.
points.name: AgFunder indexes the investment flow

points.desc: Planet Labs' high-resolution imagery, Descartes Labs' geospatial ML, and EarthDaily's field-level crop indicators supply the AI-ready observation data behind yield prediction and crop-stress detection.
points.name: The satellite layer feeds the models

points.desc: The Association of Equipment Manufacturers covers autonomous machinery, AI hardware standards, and robotics adoption across crop and livestock production.
points.name: AEM tracks the machinery standards

points.desc: The nonprofit consortium sets the open data standards that let AI models ingest feeds from tractors, drones, soil sensors, and satellites - the plumbing under everything else.
points.name: AgGateway makes the data interoperable

points.desc: The International Society of Precision Agriculture is the scientific organization connecting academic research on remote sensing and spatial analytics to commercial practice.
points.name: ISPA bridges the science and the field

points.desc: The 100 Million Farmers initiative tracks AI adoption through the lens of climate-smart and regenerative agriculture metrics globally.
points.name: WEF tracks climate-smart adoption

points.desc: Bayer's Climate FieldView and Corteva's Granular are the large digital-farming platforms turning soil, weather, and yield data into planting and input prescriptions with machine learning.
points.name: The agribusiness platforms run the prescriptions

points.desc: CNH Industrial's Raven division builds driverless tractor technology, AI path-planning, and precision application - the equipment layer beyond Deere.
points.name: CNH and Raven automate the other fleets

points.desc: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder kills weeds with computer vision and lasers instead of herbicide; Monarch builds electric driverless tractors - narrow AI shipping as farm equipment.
points.name: The pure-plays attack single problems

summary: Precision agriculture - vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, autonomous equipment - is deployed at commercial scale. Who tracks it: federal adoption data, a UN benchmarking framework, a venture index, and standards bodies, layered over the equipment giants and AI pure-plays actually shipping it.

analysis.body:
# Agriculture Sector AI Adoption Analysis

The Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey shows that adoption in agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting (NAICS 11) was suppressed in its latest report, though the prior period recorded 13.7% of firms reporting AI use within two weeks. AgFunder's investment tracking indicates that global agrifoodtech funding hit $16.2 billion in 2025, nearly flat versus the prior year at minus 3%, but with a marked shift toward companies demonstrating tangible science and clear paths to revenue. In developed markets including the US, funding showed signs of recovery in 2024, though the sector remains selective about capital allocation. Developing markets tell a different story: agrifoodtech funding in Asia-Pacific reached $4.2 billion as of October 2024, a 38% increase on the $3.1 billion raised over the same period in 2023, while African agrifoodtech raised $145 million in the first half of 2024, a 1.6% year-over-year increase after a steep 62% decline in 2023.

AI deployment in agriculture concentrates on three specific use cases: autonomous field equipment, crop monitoring and yield prediction, and precision input application. According to Climate FieldView's reported results, farmers using FieldView seed scripts saw an average increase of plus 5 bu/ac compared to users who wrote their own scripts, demonstrating measurable ROI from machine-learning-driven prescription systems. Carbon Robotics operates autonomous weeding via computer vision and lasers to eliminate chemical inputs, powered by what the company describes as a Large Plant Model trained on the world's largest agricultural dataset collected by LaserWeeders globally. Planet Labs provides daily satellite imagery and Earth data analytics serving agricultural monitoring and decision-making at continental scale, feeding the observation layer into yield prediction and crop-stress models.

The machinery and interoperability infrastructure underpins commercial deployment. AgGateway, a nonprofit, develops open data standards enabling AI models to ingest feeds from tractors, drones, soil sensors, and satellites, with traceability initiatives focused on grain and crop provenance across North America and Europe. The Association of Equipment Manufacturers convenes equipment OEMs to align on autonomous machinery standards and policies as new construction and agricultural technologies create both opportunities and regulatory challenges. The International Society of Precision Agriculture operates as the scientific bridge, connecting academic research on remote sensing and spatial analytics to commercial precision agriculture practice across its global membership and conferences.

Globally, the Food and Agriculture Organization benchmarks digital agriculture adoption and impact through its e-Agriculture community of practice and digital agriculture program, facilitating dialogue on information and communication technologies for sustainable agriculture and rural development across member nations. The USDA Economic Research Service publishes the federal measurement layer on precision-agriculture adoption across US farms, tracking variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, and autonomous equipment uptake as the authoritative series on US farmer adoption. FAO's Digital Agriculture Index specifically tracks platform adoption and real-world yield and income impact, providing a global baseline for understanding where and how digital tools are moving adoption rates.

The regulatory and risk environment remains developmental. AEM's work with equipment manufacturers centers on shaping policy and understanding data obligations as autonomous machinery becomes more prevalent, reflecting uncertainty around liability, data ownership, and standards harmonization. Funding patterns indicate that venture capital increasingly demands proven unit economics and paths to revenue rather than speculative technology bets, suggesting a maturing market where adoption decisions hinge on demonstrated yield or cost gains rather than novelty. For operators considering deployment, the strongest evidence points to seed-rate optimization and variable-rate input application as proven use cases, while broader autonomous fleet adoption remains contingent on equipment compatibility, data interoperability standards, and regulatory clarity on liability and field operations.
